prompt: In a triangle $A = 35^\circ$, $a = 7$ and $b = 9$. Two triangles are possible. Find the OBTUSE value of angle $B$, in degrees, rounded to one decimal place.
hint: Start with the Law of Sines: $\frac{\sin B}{9} = \frac{\sin 35^\circ}{7}$.

hints.text: Start with the Law of Sines: $\frac{\sin B}{9} = \frac{\sin 35^\circ}{7}$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up on the last step alone: if the calculator had returned $B = 30^\circ$, the obtuse angle with the very same sine is $180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ$. Your problem is the Law of Sines followed by exactly that subtraction.
The obtuse partner has the same sine: $180^\circ - 47.5^\circ = 132.5^\circ$.

explanation: Law of Sines: $\frac{\sin B}{b} = \frac{\sin A}{a}$, so $\sin B = \frac{9\sin 35^\circ}{7} \approx 0.73745$.
The calculator gives the acute answer, $B \approx 47.5^\circ$.
Sine is also positive in the second quadrant, so $B = 180^\circ - 47.5^\circ = 132.5^\circ$ has the very same sine.
Check it is legal: $35^\circ + 132.5^\circ = 167.5^\circ < 180^\circ$, so the obtuse triangle really exists.

alternativeExplanations.title: Both triangles, side by side
steps: Triangle 1: $B \approx 47.5^\circ$, so $C \approx 97.5^\circ$ — a tall, open triangle.
Triangle 2: $B \approx 132.5^\circ$, so $C \approx 12.5^\circ$ — a long, flat sliver.
Both have $A = 35^\circ$, $a = 7$ and $b = 9$, which is exactly why the SSA case is called ambiguous.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap is reporting $47.5^\circ$ and stopping, because that is the number the calculator displayed.
$\arcsin$ only ever returns angles from $-90^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, so it is structurally incapable of showing you an obtuse answer — it is not wrong, just incomplete.

Whenever you find an angle with the Law of Sines in an SSA problem, compute $180^\circ$ minus your answer and test whether it still fits under $180^\circ$ with the given angle. Here it does, giving $132.5^\circ$.
